predecessors.name: Union of Burma (Myanmar)
predecessors.text: the country round Ho Mong (Homein), the Mong Tai Army's headquarters 'near the border of Mae Hong Son Province': a 60 km circle cut to Shan State; the pages give no area

successors.name: Union of Burma (Myanmar)
successors.text: the country round Ho Mong (Homein), the Mong Tai Army's headquarters 'near the border of Mae Hong Son Province': a 60 km circle cut to Shan State; the pages give no area

successors.name: Wa State
successors.text: the Thai-border country the UWSA later occupied 'north and south of Kengtung' (Mong Tai Army page): a 75 km circle at Mong Hsat cut to Shan State; same region as the wa-state dossier's southern area

successors.name: Shan State National Army
successors.text: the village of Hsipaw (22.617 N, 97.283 E) 'where 8,000 fighters under the command of Colonel Yod Kan and Dae Wain retreated' and renamed themselves the Shan State National Army: a 40 km circle cut…

ledger.x: 1985: the Mong Tai Army is founded in the Shan hills.
1985: the insurgency in the Shan hills; Homein 'hosted several Shan insurgent groups' from 1985 (Homein page).
1987: the army is 'officially renamed to the MTA'; its declared goal was 'ultimately independence for Shan State'.

1995-07: Yod Kan and Dae Wain break away after a dispute on 7 July 1995: 'On 7 July 1995, an internal dispute broke out within the Mong Tai Army'; '8,000 fighters under the command of Colonel Yod Kan and Dae Wain retreated into the village of Hsipaw' and 'renamed themselves the Shan State National Army'; around 3,000…
1996: the Wa take the Thai-border country.
1996-01: the Mong Tai Army's war with Rangoon ends.
1996-01: the Mong Tai Army is dissolved when Khun Sa gives up control of his army.

wars.name: Mong Tai Army insurgency
wars.outcome: Khun Sa surrendered on 5 January 1996 (Khun Sa page; the MTA page says the majority surrendered in 1995) and the UWSA occupied the border country; the Shan State National Army split off at Hsipaw in July 1995.

certainty.note: A hill insurgent base with no recorded boundary.
